utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we invite the Prosecution to continue the examination of Witness 58, I'd like to briefly and quickly deal with a few matters. First, order of witnesses. I do understand that -- let me just -- not knowing whether matters will change. The witness at present testifying is Witness 58. The next witness would be Witness 19, if I understood well, Mr. Re. Is that 19 from the list ... No, no, no, I'm making a mistake. The next one would be witness 9, and the witness after that would be, then, Witness 19. Is that ... And then if there would remain any time, although the Prosecution is not in a position to cross-examine the witness, that they reluctantly would accept that the Chamber, in order to avoid whatever gap, to have Witness 8 as the witness to testify after that. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Witness 19 would be the witness' pseudonym, who would be followed by witness number 8 -- I'm sorry. Sorry, the confusion is between the order -- the witness number on the list and the witness pseudonym in relation to the pre-trial protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm talking now about the tentative order of testimony, which -- the next witness would be Witness number 64, tentative order of testimony, as filed, number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then after that, we'd have sequence number -- yes, I'm -- sequence number 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which -- is that -- and that's witness with pseudonym 19 and Witness number 88. Three numbers for one witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one was Witness number 27 in order of testimony, who is Witness 87 and has the pseudonym Witness 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have a different first name for that witness, 27. First name starts with an A; whereas 29, first name starts with an R.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would be 27?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That was in the proposed order of testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that's pseudonym 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness number 87. That's different from what I had on my list, and I see the Defence being rather confused as well. You sort that out during -- that witness, you sort it out during the next break, so that all parties have a similar witness on their mind. And then finally, of course, we have the issue with the witness who was in the tentative order of witnesses number 8, where there seems to be disclosure issues, where the Defence would be reluctant even to see -- to hear him testifying this week, but at least not -- would be in a position to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We were able to make some progress by agreement on the handling of that witness, and subject, of course, to the Trial Chamber's views, the proposal is that he would not be called in chief before Thursday but that the Defence would then be in a position, if the evidence-in-chief completed within Thursday, to move directly to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that would mean that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We could hear the witness from Thursday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And even -- well, the cross-examination could take place on either later Thursday or Friday. Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think Mr. Re --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He's been scheduled in chief for two hours, so that would mean the cross-examination could even start on Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's quite possible. And I think Mr. Re may have other crime base witnesses potentially lined up as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then you tried to agree on whether we're talking about witness with pseudonym 4 or 19, that is, the order of testimony number 27 or 29, and Witness number 87 or 88, it's all which one we could expect.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. 29 was first, followed by 27. I indicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Followed by 27, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. I am referring -- when I talk about these numbers, I'm referring to the list we filed on the 2nd of March of this year --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- which I thought was the definitive consolidated list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Might I also raise at this point, and I did speak to my -- at least one Defence lawyer on the weekend and sent a letter to the others in this -- or an e-mail in these terms: At the moment, in terms of witness preparation and catching up and ensuring we have the smoothest flow, the proceedings may benefit if we didn't sit on Friday this week, which would allow the Prosecution to get all the crime base witnesses together and then do the others in perhaps a -- "logical" is probably the wrong word, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, I do understand, and, of course, finally you make your -- you make your assessments of what is most efficient. At the same time, Friday is four hours in court available to the Prosecution to present its case. I mean, dates not sitting are still part of time available for the Prosecution to present its case. It's four hours from 125, unless there are very specific reasons. But usually non-sitting means time available to present evidence which is not used.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I understand that. But Your Honours saw last week there were some difficulties which I foreshadowed earlier about having all the witnesses here and in an order in which they were coming. Your Honour realises that -- the Bench realises that three witnesses were scheduled for last week and this week just didn't arrive. The difficulty that's presented us with is having to bring other witnesses forward before we were in the best position, and the Defence of course, to examination-in-chief and cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's first see what we achieve this week, and then let's see how far we come until Friday, and then we'll further discuss whether it's -- your suggestion will be followed or whether we'll not take into account that Friday. Yes. Then anything else as far as the order of witnesses is concerned? If not, there is a request for a subpoena that was filed on the 9th of March; the witnesses, it's suggested, to appear between the 19th and 23rd of March. I understand the subpoena to say, You, Witness, you should be here at that and that time. And how much time the testimony takes is another matter. And not -- of course, you can indicate that it will take several days or more than one day or -- but are you able to -- do you think that it's manageable to get a witness here on the 19th? Because if you say he has to be here between the 19th and the 23rd of March, that means that it must be feasible to get him here on the 19th.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution is in a position to facilitate as best as it can someone coming within a week. However, we're asking the Trial Chamber to -- and, of course, we wouldn't expect you to do otherwise, but to take a practical approach here in terms of issuing of subpoenas, because there's obviously a time delay, and we have no control over how subpoenas are issued and when a person is actually brought to The Hague. So in that respect, what we're -- what we're more after is a range of dates when the person comes to the court and then is told he'll testify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But when do you expect him to arrive? The 22nd, would that be good enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Um.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then he failed to be here on the 19th, and he's therefore not obeying to the subpoena, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The 22nd, the 23rd, we have the British military expert scheduled to testify. That's a date we can't -- we can't move that forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I want you to think about what you expect from a witness. If I say to a witness, you're asked to appear between the 19th and the 23rd of March, would that mean that could he come in on the 22nd and say, Here I am, and has he then obeyed to the order or not, or -- I mean, why not find the first day on which you both want him to be here and consider it possible that he is here, reasonably possible, and then say, That's when you have to be here, and then we'll hear your testimony in that -- on that day and/or the days immediately after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I must have misunderstood what Your Honour was saying. Now I recall, we did say between those dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What we mean is to appear on the first date, to appear in The Hague before the Tribunal on the first date --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- and to testify either on that date or the dates within that range.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It being, in a sense, a first-return date to ensure the witness is here, and then saying, depending on some exigencies, but other witnesses are here and testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We want you to testify within that range of dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So you want him to be subpoenaed to arrive on the 19th, to be in court on the 19th, and then to stay as long as he's needed on the dates after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, that's clear. Yes. Do you think it's feasible - today it's the 12th - 19th, any serious problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution's perspective.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but if the witness has a problem, the Prosecution has a problem as well because the witness is not here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The problem is the witness might come voluntarily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say I'm confident that this witness could be here on 19th, in view of all practical problems, travel documents, arrangements, et cetera, then we might consider to issue. And if you say, Well, could be that there's a chance of 60 per cent that he'll not be able to be here on the 19th but on the 20th, then rather subpoena him for the 20th. That's the kind of assessment I'm seeking.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can never give any sort of guarantee that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking for a guarantee. I'm asking about an assessment. I mean, if you say, it would be quite extraordinary if we did not manage to get this and this and this on the 19th, it would be really -- well, if not really exceptional, then at least unusual that we would not be able to manage that within one week, then no problem. If you say, Well, there's a 50 per cent chance that he'll make it, then we have to think about whether this is a wise thing to do or whether to take more time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I have put all the information before the Court that I possibly can about this witness. We can facilitate the issuing of travel documents, if necessary, before then, and we can facilitate the transfer of those documents to the Serbian authorities to ensure that they're -- that they're issued in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just can't take it any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Of course, what we'd like to hear is if you say 90 per cent chance that we'll make it or that the witness will make it, then it's different from a 30 per cent chance. The Chamber is not very much inclined to issue subpoenas on a 30 per cent chance; whereas the Chamber might be well inclined to say, Well, if there's a -- well, most likely he'll make it, then, of course, you could consider to issue a subpoena for that day. So what I'd like to hear from you, on the basis of your experience, if you say, Well, most likely he'll be able to do it, or serious doubts as to whether ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I can't take it beyond saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear. I don't get an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't give you an answer. I cannot give you a percentage of whether he will come or not. I can say we will facilitate it and do everything we possibly can, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not blaming you, but -- okay, you say I can't answer your questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please note the overlap for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Pretty high chance of it if Your Honours were to issue it today. I can't -- beyond that, I can't give you a percentage. We can do everything we can humanly do to get him here next week, on the Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. There is not a matter pending? That is, the Defence has not taken a position, I think, in relation to the subpoena requested for -- is there any objection requested or would you need more time to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: There is no opposition to a subpoena application as far as Mr. Haradinaj is concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I see two times nodding no; so therefore, it's still possible, Mr. Re, to consider issuing a subpoena today. Of course, the Defence not asking for more time. We'll consider the matter. Yes. Last issue: The 2nd of March notification of clarification of paragraph 89 of the indictment and request for leave to add a clarification. The Chamber is aware that the Defence has another two days to respond. Do you at all intend to reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see one time -- also nodding no?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harvey, you joined that, so that is clear, so the therefore Chamber will not wait for a reply before considering the request. These were the procedural matters at this moment. Mr. Re, are you ready to continue the examination-in-chief of Witness 58?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are the protective measures in place, Madam Registrar; that is, face distortion and pseudonym? Then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom. What was not on my list is that there was another request, which is very recent, for protective measures. What -- the Chamber would not grant two weeks for the Defence to respond, but when do you think you could respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can respond orally today. The application is opposed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that's on behalf of all three?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Are we speaking with regard to the most recent application?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, that application is opposed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: By all three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By all three. That's clear. Then we'll take time later this afternoon to look at the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Does the Chamber at any point wish to have some oral presentation with regard to that opposition or ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But since we now invite the witness to come in, we'll do that at another moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 58. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony last week, Friday. Mr. Re will now continue his examination.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness 58.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you remember back to Friday, I'd asked you a lot of questions about what happened in May, late May, 1998, when you and your family went to the mill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And we got to the point where you were telling the Court about a person called Aslan who was mistreating members of your family?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before I go further on that, I want you to tell the Court, tell the Judges, what was the weather like when all that was happening?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was raining and cold.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you describe the type of rain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Describe the rain. Was it light rain, heavy rain, spotted rain? Was it raining all the time, a little bit of the time? Clouds? What was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was raining, and it was cold.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Friday, I was asking you about this person Aslan that you saw at the mill.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he came --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop, stop. Did you know Aslan before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you know him before?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from before because he lived before you enter Gregovisht, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know whether he has another name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aslan Luluni was his name.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you saw him on that day at the mill, was he armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was. He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What weapon --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, if I might. I would ask Mr. Re not to lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm not sure how that's -- how asking whether someone is armed is actually leading a witness. There are many answers to that. You could say Yes, No, Don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Very well. I'll leave it for the moment, but I think Mr. Re understands the import of my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll leave it for the time being. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to turn off the mic after finishing because there's a lot of noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you a moment ago what weapon he had.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had all sorts of weapons, large, small. I didn't pay a lot of attention. I had a lot on my mind, the care of my kids and everything. They were crying; I was crying; my second sister-in-law was crying; all of us were crying. So I don't remember very well. I can't tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do to your sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They encircled us in a meadow before the mill, and he said, We have to search you to see whether you have some arms or something. We said, We don't have anything you might think of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, may I simply ask this: When questions like that last one are put, Mr. Re make it clear, through the appropriate form of words, which sister-in-law he is asking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, did your question cover either of them or were you specifically -- because we have -- we have Witness 38 and a second sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No names. Just refer to either the sister-in-law who's 38 or the second sister-in-law. Which sister-in-law were you referring to just then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I was talking of the two of them, for the second and -- for the elder and for the younger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was their father there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What, if anything, happened to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was trying to explain, to talk with them. They were shouting at him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who is the "they" that were shouting at them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were many. I heard only Aslan shouting. I think I told you once, there were many of them, but I didn't recognise all of them, because, as I said, I was taking care of my children and I was very scared, myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said that Aslan had searched your second sister-in-law's bag. Did Aslan do anything to the second sister-in-law's father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wanted to rape my second sister-in-law. I didn't let him. I cried. He searched her bag and then picked up the things. And I took my kids and the wife of my father-in-law and my sister-in-law and we went a little further. And I can't remember very well because I was scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said he wanted to rape your second sister-in-law. What --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question that was propounded to the witness was not answered. I understand that this is information that Mr. Re wishes to elicit, and I certainly have no objection to him proceeding to elicit information in whatever way he chooses to see fit. However, for purposes of a record that needs review, when a question is asked and an answer given is not to the question asked, it causes a great deal of confusion. And I don't want to be jumping up and saying that the answer is non-responsive, but I would appreciate it if, when such things happen, Mr. Re guide his witness in an appropriate fashion so that we don't have this occur.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is there any rule that if a witness is not very responsive to the question, that if the party questioning the witness decides, rather, to proceed than to further assist on receiving an answer, is there any rule, to your knowledge, which obliges the party to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I know of no rule which would oblige the party necessarily to do so; however, for the purposes of having an orderly transcript, one from which you, as a Chamber, can reflect and one from which we, as advocates, can argue, I think, would be of some benefit. Because if I were, at this point, with regard to this particular issue, discuss this evidence as it relates to the father-in-law, then you, as a Chamber, could rightfully criticise me with regard to the fact that there was no evidence in that regard. So what I'm trying to do is establish a basis upon which we have some kind of order. That's all I'm looking for, Your Honour, order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider to what extent it's just in the discretion of the examining party to refrain from further insisting on getting an answer on the specific question. Now, I also want to respond to an earlier matter. You said that you would not persist, you said, on whether a question to whether a certain person was armed was leading. If a witness -- Friday - and I refer you to page 883, line 17 - when talking about the KLA members said that they were armed, then I really have difficulties in understanding to what extent the witness could be seduced by a question of this leading character to introduce something the witness would not have introduced otherwise. That's really totally not understandable to me. Mr. Guy-Smith, you did not insist on the matter, so there's no ruling, but I just want to explain to you that I had difficulties in understanding the objection that you finally did not make. Mr. Re, at this moment the Chamber will not insist you on -- will not insist on you trying to get an answer to the question. We'll consider how important it is and we'll consider your duties in this respect. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said a moment ago he wanted to rape your second sister-in-law. What did he do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me about the elder or the younger? Just make it clear, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The second sister-in-law, the one you referred to earlier, not Witness 38.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I told you the first day as well. I didn't allow him to rape her, because he attempted to rape her but I didn't let him, so he didn't rape her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do? What did you see him do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see him any -- I didn't see anything else. I just took my kids. They didn't do anything to her after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said he attempted to rape her. Why do you say that he attempted to rape her? What did you see that makes you say that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say they raped her. They attempted to rape her, but I didn't let him do that. I didn't say they raped; I just simply said they attempted to rape her.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he do to her that made you think that he was trying to rape her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't let him -- she put on her clothes and I took her with me, and I was crying and shouting, and I didn't let him. She put on her clothes. And you should make it clear to all that they didn't rape her; they just tried to rape her. I want to tell here the truth. I want to tell you what really happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. We understand that you just want to confine yourself to what you saw. You said, "She put her clothes on ..."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tell the Court about her clothes. You said she put them on. Were they off?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat it? I am not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Re, I can interrupt. You told that your sister-in-law put her clothes on. Could you tell us, she had taken the clothes off or someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] She put on the clothes herself. They wanted to rape her but I didn't let them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. It might be not easy for you to talk about it, because you might have, from what I understand, have found it an embarrassing situation. But this Chamber would like to hear some of -- some details. If you say, My sister put her clothes on, and you wanted to prevent her to be raped, could you tell us, she was undressed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, they didn't rape her. She was dressed. They wanted to undress her, but I didn't allow them. So I wanted to know that I didn't say they took her clothes off. Wanted to, but didn't do it, and they didn't do anything else to her. I'm telling you things which are correct, not things which didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, did they touch her in an attempt to take her clothes off or did they say to her that she had to take her clothes off? Could you give us a bit more detail on what exactly happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said so, but I didn't let her take off her clothes and she didn't take off her clothes. They only emptied her bag, to search it, but nothing else. They didn't do anything else to my second sister-in-law. I am saying to you what really happened but nothing else. And then I went a little further away with my kids and my sister-in-law and we stayed there for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let me stop you for a second. You said that is -- you said, "They didn't do anything else to my second sister-in-law." Now I'd like to move to the sister-in-law --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Witness 38. Did they -- was she all the time dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the same thing the first time. I don't know what she said, but I know only what I am saying to you. I came here to say what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps a very simple question: Did you at any moment at the mill see your sister-in-law number 38 at any moment undressed, whether voluntarily or whether forced or whether --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't pay much attention. I left for 10 or 15 minutes. This is all I wanted to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you: Would you feel ashamed if she would have been undressed? Would you find that embarrassing, even to tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I am telling you the truth. I don't know what she has said. I told you what I saw. I cannot say things which I didn't see. After staying there for a while, as I said, we took to the mountains, through the bushes, through the hedges, and then I don't know other things. I can't tell you things which I don't know, which didn't happen. What she told you, I don't know, but I am telling you what I remember. What I don't remember, I am not saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the right thing to do. Mr. Re, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if that's correct or not, but I'm telling you what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In that group of people, was anyone tied up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't paying attention. I wasn't paying attention. As I said, I was moving along a road with bushes and hedges. I was looking after my children, who were hungry, so I wasn't paying attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I asked you a little while ago what they did to your sister-in-law's father and you said they attempted to rape your second sister-in-law. Now, I want you to think only about the father. What did they do to the father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were shouting at him. They were maltreating those two. And as I said, I wasn't paying attention, really. They were maltreating them. There were a lot of people and I don't remember everything exactly. I was ill --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Just try and focus on -- concentrate on the little thing I'm asking you, all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said they were maltreating the two of them. Now, tell the Judges about the way they maltreated the father. What did they do to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know how to describe it. I forgot part of it and time has gone by. They were shouting at him. Then they took us to a place. We stayed there in the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Stop. The father was all I'm interested in, okay? Nothing more, okay? Good-o. Now, I'm going to ask you about how long you stayed around the mill for. How long were you there for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. I don't remember exactly, but it wasn't for too long. Maybe until the 6th or 7th, or 6 or 7. I don't remember. As I said, I haven't done much school.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. When you said -- I'm just interested in the amount of time you spent there. Was it minutes, hours, days? How long did you stay around the mill for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. From 8.00 in the morning and it was then 4.00 or 5.00 or 7.00 or 8.00 when we set off towards the Jasiq mountain. This is what I know. We didn't stay long at the mill.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it your family members you told us about on Friday who went with you towards the Jasiq mountain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some Roma, a certain Jusuf, and another with his wife; then the wife of my father-in-law and nobody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about your two sisters-in-law and the children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the children and my sister-in-law, we were all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you go towards the Jasiq mountains?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we were scared. We thought we would find some peace there. We spent the night there out in the cold, in the rain, hungry, without any food. We spent the night there, then the next day, we took to the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, your question was, and I invite the witness also to listen carefully, your question was: "What about your two sisters-in-law and the children?" And then, Witness 58, in your response, you said: "And the children and my sister-in-law," not sisters-in-law. Were they both there when you went towards Jasiq mountains, or was just one of them there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both of them were. We were all together. Both of them were with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you went there because you were scared. What were you scared of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was scared because my children were crying. I wasn't feeling very well at that time. We were all feeling that way. And then we spent the night there at Jasiq mountain, and we left the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was causing you the fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of KLA. We were scared. We were hungry. We didn't have any bread or water. Nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you afraid of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by God I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was there for you to be scared of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot of KLA and I was scared. We remained there in the mountains, and as I said, we were hungry, we didn't have any food. I was scared; my children were scared; all of us were scared, because there were a lot of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you spent the night at Jasiq mountain and left the next day. Where did you go to, and who were you with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left with my entire family, my husband's family, my father-in-law, and then we in Gjocaj, near a shop or house, I don't know what it was. There, there were many of them. They wanted to fire. And a certain Gani from Istog didn't let them fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to tell the Court in more detail about what happened then, okay? But just in a moment. Did this thing, when they wanted to fire, did that happen the day after you spent the night at Jasiq mountain? Just yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was after the Jasiq mountain, after we left Jasiq mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it the next day or a different day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was the following day, the morning when we left the mountain. I don't know at what time exactly we left the Jasiq mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So the incident where they tried to fire at you, did that happen, as far as you can remember, in the morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Jasiq? Are you referring to Jasiq or Gjocaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: At Gjocaj.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They wanted to fire there, that Gani that I mentioned, he was from Istog, and he told them, Don't you dare fire, but then they said, Yes, we should fire, we should kill them at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Step by step, one thing at a time, and then everyone will know what you're talking about; all right? Firstly, was it in the morning, the afternoon, or the night, as best as you can remember?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it was in the morning, early in the morning, 6.00, 7.00, or 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went to the mountains. Gani didn't let them. We could hardly walk, and we reached Batusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did it take you, doing your best to remember, to get from the mountain to where this happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it was 7.00 or 8.00, and then it took us quite -- I don't know what time it was exactly. Maybe it was 5.00 or 2.00. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get from Jasiq mountain to Gjocaj? Did you walk, drive? How did you get there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, we went on foot. We went on foot to Batusha. We didn't have any cars. We were on foot, on mountain paths.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was it that they wanted to fire on you? I want you to describe the area you went to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're referring to Gjocaj? It was in Gjocaj where they wanted to fire. This is what I said earlier. This Gani from Istog didn't let them fire. He told them, Don't you dare, and they said, Well, these people should be killed, but then he told them, No, don't shoot, and made them move away.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to Gjocaj and what happened there. Tell the Court about what the place looked like. Were there trees? Were there houses? Was it in the mountains? Was it near a river? Whatever. Just tell the Court what the area was, what sort of landscape it was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should know that I don't know exactly what it was, whether it was a shop or a house, but I can tell you that there were a lot of them. I don't know the exact number. As I said, this Gani didn't allow them to fire, and we managed to reach Batusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Don't talk about Gani. I just want you to tell the Court where it was. You said there might be a shop or a house; okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is Gani from Istog.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it outside or inside that this attempted shooting happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to Gjocaj or somewhere else or to the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm talking about Gjocaj. All I'm talking about at the moment is Gjocaj; okay? Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. So it's all about Gjocaj. They were outside, they weren't inside. They were all outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a lot. I don't know them. I wasn't looking at them. I encircled my own children and I wasn't watching them, looking at them, at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: A lot of who? Were they civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were soldiers. They were all KLA. I don't know them, but they were a lot. So this person from Istog didn't allow them to fire and he said to them, Don't you dare imprison them or do anything to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Tell the Court about the -- what the area looked like, what the land or the earth looked like, where you were. Were there trees, mountains, rivers, fences, stones? What did the area look like? Just describe it for the Court.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was kind of a road. I wasn't paying attention whether there were apple trees or other trees around. But it was a road that takes you to Batusha. There were trees, there was a shop, there was a house, but I wasn't paying attention whether there were trees around. All I wanted to do is make this road and leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've told us a few times about the person from Istog stopping the KLA from shooting. I want you to tell the Court, to describe, where you were and where the KLA were. What happened? Firstly, how far away were the KLA soldiers from you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, three or five steps away. They weren't very far.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wanted to fire, so this person from Istog told them, Don't shoot --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. They wanted to fire. What made you think they wanted to fire? What were they doing that gave you the -- that told you they wanted to fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They directed their weapons up. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who were you there with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to go to Batusha, so all of us were there, my sisters-in-law, my father-in-law --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm after is who were the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think there's an indication from behind that there may be a translation problem. May I make inquiries to see what it is and, if it's a significant one, to correct it in due course?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, but you're instructed not to clarify issues in the presence of the witness with her earphones off, because it might have a suggestive effect which is, of course, not -- No, no, no, the witness can -- I don't know what language Mr. Haradinaj is speaking at this moment, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: He's speaking in the English that he's capable to manage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You can consult with him. There's no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said: "All of us were there, my sisters-in-law, my father-in-law," you. Who else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some people from Junik, a Jusufa and Mihani, but they stopped them, they told them, You can stay here but they cannot. So they stopped there and we proceeded.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who did the KLA try to -- or look like they were going to shoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Us, the entire family that was with the elderly sister-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When they had --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only our family.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I interpose a slight objection at this point in time. Mr. Re has repeatedly talked about "the KLA" doing something, like shooting or attempting to do other things. There are individuals who are involved in this case. Those individuals have not been identified. I think for purposes of the trial proceedings, as well as for purposes of clarification, the use of this particular term, and I understand that there's quite an assumption being made here, but I think we need a bit more identification with regard to the individuals who were involved so that the Chamber can make a determination of whether or not the characterisation made by Mr. Re is, in fact, ultimately accurate when reviewing the entirety of the evidence. And I understand the term has been used for quite some period of time, but I think that it would be important for the Chamber to have an understanding of the identities of the individuals, or some other form of an understanding of who the individuals were who she was involved with at this point in time so that an independent determination can be made as to whether or not, in fact, this was KLA activity, which is actually something which is somewhat central to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re, until now, the witness has explained on several occasions people she didn't know but she identified for the reasons stated by her as KLA or KLA members. If we enter ever into a new -- a new context or a new group, would you please verify whether the basis on which the witness is talking about KLA is the same as she did before, or whether there's -- or whether she happened to know the persons involved. Yes. By the way, Mr. Guy-Smith, approximately I think you used something like 18 or 20 lines. I think the same could have been said in three. Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to help the Judges, you said they were all KLA. How do you know they were KLA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could recognise them because they spoke Albanian and they had the KLA insignia. There were no Serbs there. There was not a single Serb left; they had all left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Let's go back to what they did to you. You said they had weapons and your family was there. What did they say or do? Where were you and your family and where were they? Just describe those things.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about my own family or my husband's family? I think you're talking about my husband's family. We were all together. I was with my husband's family. There was this cousin of my sister-in-law and nobody else. I recounted the persons who were with us in the group. Nobody else was there. I told you what I know. I cannot tell you what I don't. What I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just tell us what happened. You said they had weapons. Your family members were there, the KLA were there. What did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were sitting around there. I don't know what they were doing. What can I tell you? They came up to us another time, saying what to do, You should do this, you should do that, and then I don't know. Then we left in the direction of Batusha.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Witness, you said a little earlier that you thought they were trying to shoot you. I want you to tell the Court about that. What did they do? Just concentrate on that area. Tell the Court what happened. What was it they did that made you think they were trying to shoot you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they wanted to shoot us. They said, Who is the family of my elder sister-in-law, we want to kill them, they said. And then this guy from Istog, he said, No, you shouldn't shoot them, and they didn't. And then we left the place. This is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were they doing with their weapons when they wanted to shoot you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What were they doing? I don't know what they were doing. They threatened us and then I explained to you that this man from Istog saved us. And then through the mountain route, we went to Batush and they didn't fire at us. Then the army in Batush took us to Gjakov, and then nobody else did anything to us, because nobody allowed them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: She's repeating the same sentence twice, three times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, let me try to clarify the issue. You told us that they said that they wanted to shoot you. Was it just by words or did they do anything more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't do anything because that guy didn't allow them. They wanted to shoot at us but they did not. This person said, No, no, you should not kill them, and then they left us alone and we left in the direction of Batush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I then take it that they did not point their weapons at you when they were stopped.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They didn't do anything to us and we left in the direction of Batush mountain. They left us alone. We walked through the mountain and then arrived in Batush. This is all I remember, what I'm telling you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Judge Orie, he's the Judge in the middle, he just asked you if they -- he asked you whether they pointed their guns at you. I want you to concentrate on that. You said they had weapons. Did they --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They pointed the guns, but this person did not allow them to shoot at us. And then they lowered their weapons and didn't do anything to us. This is a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you remember --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps I'd like to verify that. I earlier said: "May I take it that they did not point the weapons to you," but you now seem to say that they did point the weapons to you but they were stopped to do anything further by this person. Important is, if you just look at me for a second, if you'd just look at me for a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please look at me. If this is a weapon, my arm, was it like that, or did they point it at you and they were stopped from shooting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They pointed their weapons. Maybe you didn't listen to me carefully. I said to you before. But they lowered their weapons only when this person told them not to shoot at us. Maybe you didn't understand me right. I am repeating it to make it clear. And then they left us alone after that, and then we followed this mountain route and went to Batush, and then the Serbian army took us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Maybe you can demonstrate. Can you stand up? Yes, up. Just hold the guns like the KLA did at your family. Just demonstrate what they did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this, and then this guy yelled at them. We were sitting like this. He did not let them shoot at us, and they didn't do anything to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said they pointed their guns. Show the Judge, who just asked you the questions, with your arms, as if you're holding a gun. Pretend you've got a gun in your hand; all right? Now, what did they do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like this. They wanted to shoot, and then this guy shouted at them, and then they first raised their weapons and pointed them at us, and then they lowered their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just do that pointing bit again. I want to describe what you just did.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wanted to fire at us. This is how they made their hands. And they rose their arms up, and then they lowered them again, and then they let us alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the record reflect that it was a sort of a classical shooting position from the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's difficult, because there's not only face distortion but also body distortion, to some extent. I think that it's sufficiently reflected that the witness showed with her hands that at least they went up in a -- I wouldn't say a fully horizontal position, but at least at some moment there was some kind of a horizontal movement, and then arms went down again. That's the most we can say. Mr. Re, you may proceed. I don't know how much time you still think you'd need for -- to finish your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Hopefully not long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please sit. Now, how many of them pointed their weapons at you in the way you've just demonstrated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I tell you? I don't remember very well. They were a couple of steps away from us. Twenty minutes, I don't know. It's a long time since then, and I was worried about my children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When I say numbers, are we talking about 1, 2, 10, 20, 100, 5? How many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The family of my elder sister-in-law?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No. How many KLA men pointed their weapons at you? More than one?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were many. No, no, they were many. I don't know. I don't know how many exactly they were. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, next, was your family and you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I'd like to receive an answer to your last question. You said there were many KLA men. Could you tell us how many among them did point their weapons at you and/or your family? Did they do it, all? Was there ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were four, five, ten, I don't know. But I do know that there were several. And a long time has passed since then, but I cannot exactly tell you how many. Three to five. I didn't pay much attention. I was frightened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When they were doing this, pointing their guns at you, wanting to shoot you, where was your family? Was it sitting, standing, kneeling? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were standing. And then they didn't take us long. They allowed us to leave. Maybe this all lasted 10 or 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why were you standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were about to leave from Jasiq, to leave that place, because we were frightened because they were shouting and yelling, and then we left. That guy did not let them fire at us, and then they let us go.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When they were pointing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re, just for your information, the Chamber wants you to finish the examination-in-chief before the break, and that's another nine minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm trying very hard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Just for you to know that the Chamber has decided that it should not take any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When they were pointing their guns at you, you said you were standing. Were you standing in a circle, in a line, in clusters, together? Just describe how you were standing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were lined up.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All our family.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. How were you lined up? How did you come to be lined up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were lined up. We were on the point of leaving, and then they did what they did. They prevented us from leaving, wanted to fire at us. This person did not let them fire at us, and they stopped from firing. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did they line you up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they did. They told us, We want to kill you, all of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this is the family of -- they mentioned the name of my elder sister-in-law. We want to kill all of you because she worked with the Serbs. And then this man from Istog came in and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just talk about the lining up. What did they do so that you got lined up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wanted to fire at us. I explained to you for the umpteenth time: That person did not allow them to shoot and then they let us go through the mountains, in the direction of Batush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Stop.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We stumbled and we walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop. Just the line-up. Did they tell you to stand in line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They said, You should line up, all you members of the family of my elder sister-in-law, because we want to kill you. And that man from Istog did not let them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you feel when they lined you up and held their guns at you, wanting to shoot you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard them saying, We must kill the entire family. There were many of them, but this man did not allow them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. That's not what I'm asking you, though. I'm asking you how you felt.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Me? How did I feel?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that, nothing happened to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What were your feelings at the time? Good, bad, something in between?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What can I say? I wasn't feeling well. I was sick. I was crying. I was worried over my young children.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your children with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were with me. Yes, we were all together, the entire family.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were they in the line of people the KLA wanted to shoot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of us. I held them by the hands and held them close to myself, and they were crying, they were scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do this very quickly. Where did you go to after this, after the man from Istog intervened? Where did you go? Just tell us quickly where you went.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went through mountains, to Batush, to the Batusha mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you run into the Serbian -- did you find the Serbian army there and did they look after you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the KLA? No. We walked through the mountains. It was a hard walk. We heard fired shots but we kept walking and went to Batush.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, finally, I want to ask you about your house in Ponosevac and your sister-in-law's, that's 38's place, in Junik. Have you been back to Ponosevac or Junik since that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go back, neither to Ponoshevc or Junik. Never went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I was scared. Because she worked, as I said, with the Serbs and I didn't go back. And I don't know whether the houses have been burned or not. I know nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why were you scared to go back? What did you fear would happen if you went back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was scared where to go. They didn't let you go back. Maybe they were burned. I don't know. I was simply scared and refused to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have any members of your family gone back to Ponosevac, to your houses there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't. No one went back. I stayed in Gjakov. We didn't go back there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you leave Kosovo? Sorry, when did you leave Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Over five years, five years and five months.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you now living in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you seeking asylum or refugeeship there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, asylum.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say you were scared and refused to go back, what are you scared -- what were you scared of? Why were you scared to go back to Ponosevac? What was causing you the concern about going back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where should I go? Where could I go back? All my family was with me, so why should I go back? Where could I go back to? We couldn't live there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why couldn't you live there anymore?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have any business going there. Nobody from my family lives there. Why should I go? I have no business to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why are you seeking asylum in Switzerland? What's the reason for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am with my family. I have no place to go now that the houses are burned. I'm not with my husband, with my children. Where can I go? Where do you think I can go? There is no return for me there. There is no place for me there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Re. Witness 58, it's time for a break. After the break, you'll be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence. We'll resume at ten minutes past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will give, first of all, a decision in relation to Witness 58. This is a decision on protective measures for Witness 58. On the 9th of March of this year, the Prosecution and the Defence collectively requested protective measures for a witness who had appeared to testify without any pre-arranged protective measures. On the same day, the Chamber orally granted a pseudonym for the witness, this being number 58, as well as face distortion. The Chamber hereby gives its reasoning for this decision. The party seeking protective measures for a witness must demonstrate an objectively grounded risk to the security or welfare of the witness or the witness's family, should it become known that the witness has given evidence before the Tribunal. In the present case, it has come to the attention of the Chamber that clear and direct threats have been made towards family members of the witness. The Trial Chamber accepts that there is a risk that if the identity of the witness were to be made public, physical harm might result to the witness's family. The Trial Chamber therefore granted the requested pseudonym and face distortion. This concludes this decision. The other decision is an oral decision on the Prosecution's motion of the 7th of March, 2007. It is the Prosecution's motion for protective measures for Witnesses 4 and 19, filed on the 7th of March. In its motion, the Prosecution requests the retention of the assigned pseudonyms and the assignment of face and voice distortion. The Chamber has been informed by the three Defence counsel that they do not oppose the application. In its motion, the Prosecution argues that the witnesses' family still lives in the territory and that they face a serious risk of harm if the witnesses' identity would be made public. The Chamber is satisfied that should the witnesses' identity be made public, physical harm might result to the witnesses' family. The Trial Chamber therefore grants the Prosecution's request for the retention of the assigned pseudonyms and the assignment of face and voice distortion. This concludes the Trial Chamber's decision on protective measures for Witnesses 4 and 19. Before asking Madam Usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, as guidance for the Defence in relation to Witness 58, the Chamber informs the Defence that the Chamber will consider her testimony in relation to other evidence presented in relation to the counts 1 and 2. And the Defence is invited to keep in mind and to be aware that the Chamber, perhaps unlike a jury, is capable to distinguish between fake and precise evidence, is capable of making a distinction between signs of consistency and inconsistency, or whatever is important to consider when considering evidence, even if the attention of the Chamber would not be specifically drawn to every single aspect of this kind. This is just for guidance of the Defence. Then, Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, you'll first be examined by Mr. Emmerson, who is counsel for Mr. Haradinaj. Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 58, I'm asking you questions from this side of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, that's Mr. Emmerson, who is going to ask questions to you. He's standing now. Could you please look at him so that there's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know him. No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to know him. But if you look at Mr. Emmerson, then you know at least who is putting questions to you. Mr. Emmerson is standing over there; yes? So if you look at him when he puts questions to you, then you have at least some --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's clear. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 58, I have just got one or two questions for you, and I shouldn't be very long in asking you questions. Can I just emphasise at the outset, you have said on a number of occasions that you are telling us what you personally saw, and I'm not going to ask you about things that you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know him. No, no, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, let me explain to you what happens in this courtroom. You earlier have met with the counsel for the Prosecution. You have been interviewed by them. We are the Judges, so we'll hear your evidence because we finally will have to decide this case. Now, just as the Prosecution puts questions to you, counsel for the Defence, even if you don't know them, are entitled to put questions to you as well. The Prosecution may have asked questions which --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they can ask questions, but I can only speak of things I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that goes without saying, and they will ask you about things you know. And perhaps if you slightly turn to Mr. Emmerson, then it's -- then we all know that you understand that Mr. Emmerson is questioning you and that you are giving responses to his questions. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, Witness 58, can I make it clear, I am not going to ask you any questions about things you did not see. I'm not going to ask you any questions about things that other people in your family may have said to you. I just want to ask you questions about what you personally saw; all right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never seen him. I don't remember seeing him.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just put your questions, Mr. Emmerson. That might be the best way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I ask you this, first of all: When you went to the mill with your family, did anybody force you --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, do we have a translation for that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did not receive a translation. I don't know whether the translators --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You just said something. Could you please repeat it, because the interpreters could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember him. I don't know him. Maybe he was there, but I didn't see him. I don't know him. I haven't seen him. Maybe he was there, but I didn't see him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, I don't know who you're talking about. It might be that you are talking about Mr. Haradinaj and that you have not seen him there, I do not know. But carefully -- carefully --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't see him and I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you first would be so kind to listen to the questions put to you by Mr. Emmerson, and I don't think at the moment that he's asking the question you gave a response to already. I think that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may speak but I don't know him. I have never seen him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 58, if you first listen to the question that Mr. Emmerson will put to you, then tell me whether you understand that question; if you understand it, then you can respond to that question. It might be something totally different from what you think he might ask you. Mr. Emmerson, could you please ask your first question?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Witness 58, the question I was asking you was, when you went with your family to the mill, did anybody force you to go there, or did you and your family choose to go there for your own safety?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were told to leave the house, and we left and went to the mill. I don't know him. I've never seen this person. Maybe he was there, but I haven't seen him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's stop there. Let's stop there for a moment, Witness 58. You said: "We were told to leave the house, and we left and went to the mill." We're not talking about a specific person at this moment at all. Did you choose, yourself, because you felt unsafe, to go to the mill, or were you told by whomever that that's where you had to go? Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They came and they told us that we had to leave and we left. I don't know who they were. I don't remember. There were a lot of them. We left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think it's right, Witness 58, that it was your choice, the family's choice, to go to the mill for safety; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not ourselves, but they told us that we had to leave and we left. They were shooting, the windows were broken, and we left. They said that all of us had to leave and we left. They forced us to leave. I don't know who they were. I don't remember them. I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But did anybody specifically tell you that you had to go to the mill rather than somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I'm saying. They came, the KLA, and they said that we had to leave that place and we left. They said to us, There's no place for you here, you have to leave, and we left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I again try to focus your attention on the following: Mr. Emmerson was asking you, when they told you that you had to leave, you can then do that in several ways. You can say, You have to leave and you have to go there, for example, to the mill, or to say, You have to leave; choose where you want to go. Now, what was it? Did they leave it to you to decide where to go, or did they say you have to leave, and you have to go to the mill?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said, Leave this place, and then we went to the Tofaj place. I think that's what it's called.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've said now on a number of occasions over the last few minutes: "I have never seen this person. Maybe he was there but I didn't --"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I don't know him. That's correct, I don't know him, and that's what I said then.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who these people who came and told us to leave were.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we left. They told us to leave, but as I said, I don't know who they were. I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were at the mill, did you or any members of your family or your husband's family go inside a building at any time, or were you always outside?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Outside, outside. We stayed outside. We stayed outside. Tell them we stayed outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you left the mill area, you've told us that you walked up to the Jasiq mountain where you spent the night; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Correct. It was cold; it was raining. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when you were walking from the mill at Tofaj up to the Jasiq mountain, were both of your sisters-in-law with you at that time, walking up from the mill area to the mountain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS SST7/58 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children, the sisters-in-law, both of them, the wife of my father-in-law, my father-in-law, and we went on foot to Jasiq mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
